evidence.quote: we continue to anticipate that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate at least through late 2014.
we remain entirely prepared to take additional balance sheet actions if necessary to achieve our objectives.
Consequently, we anticipate that inflation will subsequently run at or below the Committee’s longer-run goal of 2 percent.
if the data were to come in much stronger than expected, we would adjust the guidance appropriately.
Strains in global financial markets, though less pronounced, generally, than last fall, continue to pose significant risks to the outlook.
However, at 8.2 percent, the unemployment rate remains elevated.

parsed.rationale: The Chair maintains highly accommodative policy and late-2014 guidance, keeps further balance sheet easing on the table, and emphasizes downside risks and slow labor market progress. This is tempered by his rejection of tolerating higher inflation and his note that the guidance would shift if data strengthened notably, leaving the signal moderately dovish.
